# Surface Labs

> Surface Labs is a node-based procedural PBR texture authoring tool for indie game developers. It is an independent, portable alternative to Substance 3D Designer.

Surface Labs builds complete PBR material sets (albedo, normal, roughness,
metallic, ambient occlusion and height) from a graph of GPU-evaluated nodes on a
native Rust engine. The graph is the single source, so changing an upstream
input re-renders everything after it in real time, up to 8192 x 8192 in 8-, 16-
or 32-bit float.

## Facts

- Category: node-based procedural texture and PBR material authoring tool.
- Audience: indie game developers and technical artists.
- Platforms: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iPadOS — the same app on all
  five, on a native Rust engine with Direct3D 12 (Windows), Metal (macOS,
  iPad) and Vulkan (Linux) backends.
- Packaging: portable Windows ZIP (no installer, nothing in the registry);
  signed, notarized, universal macOS build (Apple Silicon and Intel); Debian
  .deb and Arch .pkg.tar.zst on Linux; arm64 and x64 on Android.
- One project file: .surfacelabs is a single portable archive holding every
  material, subgraph, embedded image and export setting; fonts used by Text
  nodes are embedded so type renders identically on every machine.
- Input: mouse, keyboard, touch, stylus and game controllers. Full
  game-controller navigation is built as an accessibility-first alternative to
  mouse and touch.
- No account required to use it.
- Node library includes Perlin/FBM/Voronoi/Cells noise, gradients and tile
  sampler; blur, sharpen, levels, curves, warp and gradient-map filters; blend
  and channel operations; normal-from-height, curvature and AO tools; histogram
  and math nodes; plus GPU-compute Erosion (hydraulic and thermal), Flood Fill,
  Distance Field (jump flooding), Trim Sheet and Text. Custom nodes are written
  in full GLSL, compiled to a native pipeline.
- Automation: ships an MCP server (live, hosted by the running app, and a
  headless CLI, surface_lab_headless) for reading and editing projects,
  rendering nodes and exporting texture sets; every edit goes through the same
  validation as the canvas.
- Export presets: Unreal Engine, Unity (URP and HDRP), Godot and glTF /
  three.js, with correct channel packing (ORM, MetallicSmoothness, HDRP Mask
  Map) and DirectX or OpenGL normal orientation. Output as PNG, JPEG, TGA, BMP
  or OpenEXR.
- Pricing: free during early access; $10 per platform planned at the 1.0.0
  release. One-time purchase, no subscription.
